title: 7 Google AI Studio Alternatives Worth Trying in 2026
summary: Google AI Studio alternatives compared on what each free tier covers and where your app lives: Lovable, Bolt.new, Replit, v0, Agent Studio and more.
body_markdown:
Key takeaways:


- Google AI Studio is free in every available region, but the newest Pro-class models aren't on the Gemini API free tier, and outside the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, free-tier content can help improve Google's products.
- Five of the seven alternatives here have a free tier, and the two that don't start at a $5 prepaid minimum on OpenAI Platform and $19 a person a month on our Light plan, plus our $200 monthly Platform Fee.
- Build mode hosts up to 2 apps free on Google Cloud's Starter Tier for eligible personal accounts, with Cloud Run usage pricing past that, while Lovable, Bolt.new and Replit host apps in their own workspace and v0 deploys to Vercel on Free.
- Google's pricing page shows input on its Gemini 4 reasoning models, Carbon and Argon, doubling to $4 per 1M tokens on December 1, 2026, so price a move to a paid key at the new rate.


Google AI Studio is free to use, and for testing a prompt or sketching a Gemini-powered app, that's hard to beat. The search for Google AI Studio alternatives starts later: you want the newest Pro-class models, you'd rather your prompts stayed out of training, or your Build mode app has outgrown Google's free hosting and is heading for a Cloud Run bill.


This roundup compares seven options on two questions. What does each free tier cover, and where does your app live once you stop building in AI Studio? We last re-checked every free tier and price on November 13, 2026.


We put our own product, Awesomic, first because it's ours. The rest start with four browser builders,[prototyping tools](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/prototyping-tools) that host what they make, closest to Build mode first, and end with the API and console paths for people who used AI Studio as a Gemini playground.


## Why people look past Google AI Studio


To be fair to Google, the headline holds up: "Google AI Studio usage is free of charge in all available regions." People leave because the free setup stops short of their next step, for three reasons.


### The free tier stops before the newest models


The limits sit one layer down, in the Gemini API tiers that AI Studio runs on. Flash, Flash-Lite and Gemini 2.5 Pro are free there, while the newest Pro-class models, including Gemini 4 Carbon, Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, are marked "Not available" on the free tier. If your prototype needs the top model, you're on a paid key either way.


That paid key is also getting pricier, starting at the top. On December 1, 2026, input on Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon, Google's two Gemini 4 reasoning models, goes from $2 to $4 per 1M tokens and output from $10 to $20. On January 1, 2027, Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.6 Flash input rises from $0.75 to $1.50, and output from $3.75 to $7.50.


### Free-tier prompts can feed Google's products


The second reason is data. Google's pricing page says free-tier content is "used to improve our products," and paid-tier content isn't. The Gemini API terms go further: human reviewers may read free-tier input and output, and Google asks you not to submit sensitive, confidential or personal information there.


Google's free-tier line has edges, though. In the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, its Paid Services terms cover all use, AI Studio included, and an account with a linked Cloud billing account or a Workspace enterprise account counts as paid anywhere.


Google isn't unusual here. A[Stanford study](https://hai.stanford.edu/news/be-careful-what-you-tell-your-ai-chatbot) of six frontier developers (Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft and OpenAI) found that all six appear to use users' chat data to train their models by default, and some keep it indefinitely. It's a preprint on consumer chat policies, not API terms, but beside Google's own free-tier line it explains why teams want paid-tier terms first.


### Build mode hosting is free only up to a point


Build mode makes web apps (React plus Node) or native Android apps, written by the Antigravity agent. On the Google Cloud Starter Tier, an eligible personal account can publish up to 2 full-stack apps without a Cloud project or billing account of its own; Google runs them in what it calls "a no-cost, Google-managed project."


Past that allowance, or on a Workspace account or one that already has a paid billing account, a Standard deployment goes to Cloud Run, where pricing "may apply based on usage." You also get two-way GitHub sync and a ZIP download, but no real-time collaborative editing, and a shared app's API calls count toward your usage.


Firebase Studio isn't a way out: it stopped taking signups on June 22, 2026 and shuts down on March 22, 2027, so it gets no entry here, and neither does an[autonomous coding agent](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/devin-alternatives) , which takes the whole job off your hands.


## The 7 best Google AI Studio alternatives


The table below swaps the usual star rating for a column you can check yourself: what each option gives you for free. Pricing shows the first paid step on monthly billing.


Awesomic brings AI agents and vetted experts into one app. Start with a prompt to build a website, app, campaign, deck or video, then switch models or bring in a vetted expert without losing the project context. AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


Read the last column against the fourth and the trade-off shows up fast: every free tier that hosts your app also limits what you can do with it.


### 1. Awesomic


**Best for:** teams that switch models per task


**Overview:** Awesomic, our product backed by Y Combinator (S21), puts AI agents and vetted human experts in one app. It isn't tied to one model family the way AI Studio's Build mode is, and it gives the app a home.


Its agents can be Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode, running models from Google, Anthropic, OpenAI or xAI, switched per task on one bill.


For hosting, each project runs on a dedicated cloud machine holding up to 1 TB, where agents run real programs and you publish a site to a live link in one click. On data, our AI providers can't train on your work, and you can switch off, from then on, our use of de-identified content to train our own AI.


**Key features:**


- A cloud computer per project, so work keeps running after you close your laptop.
- Parallel agents on one project, each in its own chat.
- More than 1,000 app connections, including GitHub, Slack and Stripe, plus a shared team keychain.


**Pricing:** AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


Human help comes on its own plans. A vetted developer through Dedicated expert gets priced on a call, while All-in-One, at $3,219 a month, covers design, copy, no-code builds and quality checks. Each plan includes a Light seat.


**Pros:** one-click publishing, experts in the same chat on an expert plan, use it from a browser tab, the macOS, Windows and Linux desktop apps, or the iOS and Android apps


**Cons:** no free tier, so on cost alone AI Studio's free usage wins, no published per-model rates or word on how hosting draws on the budget, and after you cancel, only 30 days to download your files and code


**How to start using it:**


1. Sign up on Light and open a project.
2. Describe your AI Studio prototype so the agents rebuild it.
3. Run the first task on Gemini, then try Anthropic or OpenAI.
4. Publish the result to a live link.
5. Need a developer? Add a Dedicated expert plan and hand the task over in the chat.


**Why it's a good Google AI Studio alternative:** You keep Google's models, add Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI on one bill, and the app has somewhere to run from day one.


**Final verdict:** Pick Awesomic if you've outgrown a one-family playground and want the build and the hosting in[one app](https://www.awesomic.com/) . If your budget is zero, stay on AI Studio's free usage.


### 2. Lovable


**Overview:** Of the four builders, Lovable sits closest to Build mode's chat-to-app flow: it builds web apps on a built-in Cloud backend and publishes them to lovable.app, public by default or invite-only for up to 10 people.


**Key features:**


- Built-in Cloud backend, so the app needs no separate server project.
- Git sync to GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket on every plan, Free included, which keeps an exit open at $0.
- Unlimited workspace members, Free included, so nobody pays per seat.


**Pricing:** Free costs nothing and gives 5 daily build credits capped at 30 a month, plus 20 Cloud credits and 4 AI credits a month. Pro is $25 a month with 100 monthly credits, Business is $50 a month with 100 credits, and Enterprise carries a custom platform fee.


**Pros:** Git sync and unlimited members on Free, lovable.app hosting included


**Cons:** no code editing on Free and single-file downloads only (the full ZIP is paid), credits meter everything, a Free site can be unpublished once it has gone 12 months with no visits, owner login or custom domain


**Where it fits:** Hosting is settled on day one, with 5 lovable.app domains on Free and custom domains from Pro. Code stays inside Lovable until you sync it, so connect Git early.


**Final verdict:** Choose Lovable if you want hosting handled and a Git exit that reaches GitLab and Bitbucket, not just GitHub.


### 3. Bolt.new


**Overview:** Like Lovable, Bolt.new hosts what it builds and keeps a database beside the chat, so a prototype is live from the start, and GitHub sync covers the exit.


**Key features:**


- Hosting included on Free, which removes the separate deploy step.
- Unlimited databases on Free, so data has a home from the first prompt.


**Pricing:** Free gives you 1M tokens a month with a 300K daily limit, 10MB uploads and Bolt branding. Pro is $25 a month for 10M tokens and up, with no daily limit, rollover and a custom domain. Teams is $30 per member a month, and Enterprise is custom.


**Pros:** free-plan hosting and databases, private projects at $0, token rollover once you pay


**Cons:** free tokens don't roll over, bigger projects burn more tokens per message, Free lacks custom domains and the newest AI models


**Why it made this list:** A rebuilt Build mode prototype can go live here at $0 while you decide whether it deserves a paid plan.


**Final verdict:** Bolt.new suits a small prototype that needs to be live and holding data this week.


### 4. Replit


**Overview:** Replit goes a step further, keeping hosting, a database and auth in one workspace, and it bills its Agent by effort. Its free Starter plan sits in Replit's docs, not on the pricing page.


**Key features:**


- Hosting, database and auth together, so there are fewer services to wire up.
- ZIP download plus two-way GitHub auto-sync, giving you two ways out.
- Up to 15 collaborators and 28-day database rollback on Pro.


**Pricing:** Core is $20 a month and includes up to 30 hours of chat on Free Mode, up to 60 projects and $20 toward more capable models. Pro is $100 a month with $100 toward models, and Enterprise is custom.


**Pros:** database and auth built in, two-way GitHub sync, database rollback on Pro


**Cons:** the free app goes down after 30 days, effort-based costs are hard to predict, Starter allows Lite builds only (Full build and Plan Mode need Core)


**Its real strength:** It bundles a database and auth, the parts that turn a Build mode demo into a backend project.


**Final verdict:** Go with Replit if the app needs users and stored data, and budget for Core, because the free app won't outlive its first month.


### 5. v0


**Overview:** v0 is the most front-end-focused of the four builders: it generates Next.js, React, Tailwind and shadcn code and deploys it to Vercel, even on Free. Once you connect GitHub, the repo becomes the source of truth, so the app lives in your repository and on Vercel.


**Key features:**


- Deploy to Vercel on Free, so a prototype gets a live link without Cloud Run.
- Design Mode and GitHub sync on Free.
- An option to use a ChatGPT subscription for eligible OpenAI models, for a small credit fee.


**Pricing:** New users on Free get a one-time $5 credit and 7 messages a day, and Plus is $30 per user a month with $30 in monthly credits and $2 in free daily credits on login. Business is $100 per user a month, and model rates per 1M tokens run from $0.20 input and $1.20 output on v0 Mini to $10 input and $50 output on Max Fast.


**Pros:** Vercel deploys on Free, standard Next.js output, training opt-out by default on Business


**Cons:** a small free allowance, token-metered credits, generation that pauses at zero


**What it's good at:** If your AI Studio app was mostly interface, v0's output drops into a stack many teams already run.


**Final verdict:** Choose v0 for a Next.js front end you plan to keep in GitHub, and expect to move to Plus quickly.


### 6. Agent Studio


**Overview:** Agent Studio, formerly Vertex AI Studio, is where the console and API paths start: it's Google's own prompt console inside Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI). That makes it one way to stay on Gemini with paid-tier data terms, with enterprise controls on top.


**Key features:**


- A Prompt Gallery whose "Get code" panel gives Python code or opens a Colab notebook.
- Partner models such as Claude and Llama beside Gemini.
- Agent Designer and App Builder alongside the prompt tools, both still in preview.


**Pricing:** Tokens are pay-as-you-go, and grounding is free for 5,000 queries a month, then $14 per 1,000. New Google Cloud customers get a $300 credit, but for sign-ups on or after November 16, 2026, it can't pay for Agent Studio, and it never covers partner models like Claude and Llama or Gemini API use in AI Studio. Express mode, open only to new Google Cloud users with a Gmail account, has a 90-day free tier with no billing info, within quotas.


**Pros:** Gemini with paid-tier data terms, partner models in one console, enterprise controls


**Cons:** Google Cloud project setup once you leave express mode, express mode is a Pre-GA preview at 10 requests a minute on Gemini 2.5 models, its free tier ends once billing is on


**Why it's a good Google AI Studio alternative:** It keeps your Gemini prompts and adds partner models and Google Cloud's enterprise controls, two things a paid AI Studio key doesn't give you.


**Final verdict:** Agent Studio fits if you need enterprise controls or Claude and Llama beside Gemini; for data terms alone, a paid AI Studio key is enough.


### 7. OpenAI Platform


**Overview:** OpenAI Platform is the other API path, with the Responses API and the Agents SDK. Its Agents API can run managed agents in OpenAI-hosted sandboxes, but OpenAI doesn't host your web app, so the backend and hosting are yours.


**Key features:**


- Four GPT-6 family models priced from $0.10 to $10 per 1M input tokens, so you can match model to budget.
- Batch API at 50% off for jobs that don't need an instant answer.


**Pricing:** At standard short-context rates per 1M tokens, GPT-6 Astra costs $10 input and $50 output, GPT-6.1 Sol $2 input and $10 output, GPT-6.1 Terra $1 input and $5 output, and GPT-6 Luna $0.10 input and $0.50 output. Billing is prepaid credits with a $5 minimum.


The usage tiers cap spending rather than hand out credit. The tier OpenAI calls Free comes with no money, limits you to $100 a month, and isn't supported on the GPT-6 models at all. Build raises the cap to $500 once you've bought $5, and Launch to $5,000 once you've bought $100.


**Pros:** a wide spread of model prices, Batch API discount, spend caps by tier


**Cons:** no free tier, no app builder, no web-app hosting, so where the app lives is your problem


**Why buyers shortlist it:** It's a direct swap for a developer who used AI Studio to test prompts before calling a model from their own code.


**Final verdict:** Pick OpenAI Platform if you already run your own backend and just want a different model family behind it.


## What you gain and lose by switching


Each option above answers a different reason for leaving and trades away something AI Studio gives you free, so name your reason first.


On the gain side, all four browser builders host the app without a Cloud Run service, three in their own workspace and v0 on Vercel. On data, Agent Studio adds enterprise controls, and v0's Business plan opts you out of training by default.


On the loss side, you give up AI Studio's free usage in every available region and, once any 90-day express window ends, the no-cost Gemini models listed earlier.


Code access is another loss to check builder by builder. Build mode gives you a ZIP and two-way GitHub sync, Replit and Bolt.new offer both, v0 syncs to GitHub and downloads a ZIP, and Lovable syncs to GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket but downloads single files only on Free, a trade-off we weigh in[Lovable alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/lovable-alternatives) .


## How much Google AI Studio alternatives cost


The useful comparison is what the first paid step costs and what it adds over $0. Google AI Studio is in the first row as the baseline you're leaving.


For current Awesomic plans and capabilities, see[the pricing page](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


Of the seven, the Google AI Studio alternatives free to start are Lovable, Bolt.new, Replit, v0 and Agent Studio, and each one fences that free use differently: by credits, tokens, messages, app lifetime or a 90-day window.


Per-token prices keep falling.[Epoch AI](https://epoch.ai/data-insights/llm-inference-price-trends) found that the price to reach GPT-4's performance on PhD-level science questions fell 40x per year, and the drop ranged from 9x to 900x a year across tasks. That's measured per token at fixed capability, though, and frontier prices can still rise, as Google's December 1 increase shows.


Long chats also cost more at the same per-token rate, because the token count keeps growing. One commenter on[a January r/Bard thread](https://www.reddit.com/r/Bard/comments/1qnk9fq/are_there_alternatives_to_gemini_ai_studio_with/) said AI Studio's cost counter showed about $2 per prompt roughly 20 messages into a long chat on Gemini's Pro model, since each prompt resends the whole history. Builders meter usage too: v0's credits are token-metered, one reason people compare[v0 alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/v0-alternatives) .


## Where your app lives after you leave AI Studio


A deployed Build mode app runs on Google Cloud, not inside AI Studio, either within the free Starter Tier allowance or on Cloud Run usage you pay for. The real question is where you edit and host it next, and moving to a builder usually means rebuilding from a description or working from a synced repo, not uploading the exported code.


Here's the order that keeps the app live while you move it:


1. Save a copy of the code with two-way GitHub sync or the ZIP download.
2. Pick the new home: a builder's own hosting, Vercel through v0, or your own server for an API-only path.
3. Rebuild or reconnect the app there, keeping a Gemini key live until the new setup is tested.
4. Check the data terms on the new plan before real customer data goes in.
5. Take the Google Cloud deployment down only after the new link has served real traffic.


If the prototype is turning into something with paying users, planning the wider[SaaS product development](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/saas-product-development) work now saves a second migration later.


## Mistakes that make the switch expensive


Most bad switches come from reading the headline and skipping the detail under it, like these:


- Taking an Android-targeted Build mode project to a builder before checking that it supports Android.
- Testing with customer data on a free-tier Gemini key, which Google's human reviewers may read in most regions.
- Moving to Agent Studio for a $300 Free Trial credit that, for sign-ups from November 16, 2026, no longer covers it, or running Claude or Llama, which the credit never covered.
- Running production traffic on Agent Studio's express mode, which is still a preview with a low per-minute request cap.


Each is cheap to avoid once you know it's there. The slower mistake is spending a month of credits on a full product before anyone has used the prototype. A small first version still has to look intentional, though, a point our digest on[rethinking the MVP](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/design-digest-34-rethinking-the-mvp-spacial-design-importance-of-taste) makes.


## How to choose based on what you used AI Studio for


What you did in AI Studio predicts the right alternative better than any feature list.


### You used Build mode to ship web apps


Lovable, Bolt.new, Replit and v0 all take a prompt to a hosted app. Choose Replit if you need a database and auth, Bolt.new if you want hosting and unlimited databases on the free plan, Lovable if your repos live on GitLab or Bitbucket, and v0 if the app is mostly a Next.js front end.


### You used AI Studio as a Gemini playground


A playground habit doesn't need a builder. People in the January r/Bard thread mentioned above, hit by daily request limits even on a paid Google subscription, were told to use an API key or a wrapper like OpenRouter, since AI Studio is "just an interface for Gemini API." A paid key is the smallest step, Agent Studio adds enterprise controls and partner models, and OpenAI Platform brings another model family.


### You were really building a marketing site


Some AI Studio prototypes are landing pages in disguise. If you need a company site rather than an app, hiring[website design help](https://www.awesomic.com/web-design) is often quicker than prompting one into shape.


## Pick your exit by what broke first


If model limits or data terms pushed you out, try the fix inside AI Studio first: a paid Gemini key opens the newest Pro-class models and puts your content on paid terms. Leave only for what a key can't change. If hosting past Google's free allowance did it, pick a builder that hosts and test its free tier this week before you pay.


For enterprise controls or partner models on Gemini, choose Agent Studio, and for another model family behind your own backend, choose OpenAI Platform. Whichever you pick, read its training terms first.


## FAQ


### Are any Google AI Studio alternatives free?


Five of the seven here have a free tier: Lovable, Bolt.new, Replit, v0 and Agent Studio. Each limits it differently, from Lovable's 30 build credits a month to Replit's single app that goes down after 30 days, so check which limit you'd hit first.


### Is Google AI Studio really free?


Yes, AI Studio usage is free in all available regions, and Gemini 2.5 Pro, Flash and Flash-Lite cost nothing on the API's free tier. You'll need a paid key for the newest Pro-class models, and free-tier prompts can be used to improve Google's products unless you're in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK. Eligible personal accounts get two Build mode apps hosted free, with Cloud Run rates after that.


### Can I keep using Gemini after I leave AI Studio?


Yes. The simplest route is the Gemini API with your own paid key. Agent Studio, part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, also serves Gemini on pay-as-you-go pricing with paid-tier data terms, and first-timers on Google Cloud who sign in with Gmail can use its 90-day free express mode. The $300 Free Trial credit stops covering Agent Studio for anyone who signs up from November 16, 2026.


### What happens to my Build mode app when I stop using AI Studio?


Your deployed app sits on Google Cloud rather than in AI Studio, on the Starter Tier's free allowance or on paid Cloud Run usage. To move it, save the code through GitHub sync or the ZIP download, rebuild or reconnect it on its new host, and only then take the old deployment down.


### Is Firebase Studio still an option?


No. Firebase Studio closed signups and new workspaces on June 22, 2026, and the service shuts down on March 22, 2027, deleting any remaining data. Google now steers its users toward Antigravity and Google AI Studio.
